title: Prepare a 7-day content calendar for Zedu
description: Develop a structured seven-day content calendar that outlines the proposed content activities for the campaign across the selected social media platforms. The calendar should demonstrate a clear publishing strategy, with content planned to support brand awareness, audience engagement, product education, lead generation, or other approved marketing objectives. Each entry should align with the overall campaign direction and reflect the needs, interests, and behaviours of the intended audience.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Build the week from assets we already plan to publish, so the calendar points at real things
acceptedWorkstreams.description: A calendar fails when it promises content that does not exist. Start by listing what is already scheduled or likely to be ready this week from the project's other goals - the 12-post blog plan, the product pages, the help-centre answers, release notes - then build the seven days around items that will genuinely be live, each post linking to a real URL that returns 200 on the day. For each day: the objective (awareness, engagement, product education or lead), platform, the asset it points at, the copy, and who posts it. Anything not yet ready is marked as a placeholder with the date it becomes usable. Deliverables: the seven-day table, the asset list behind it with links, and a short note on what is blocked.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: One week built from problems operators actually post, each post tied to one real feature and one tracked link
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Make each day answer a problem bootcamp operators and course leads have described publicly, using the operator problem bank and objections work already done in this project, so the week isn't generic. Plan: 1) pick 7 problems (for example questions buried in chat, the week-3 drop-off, files lost in WhatsApp) and match each to one feature checked in the app's code, so no post promises something the app can't do; 2) for each day give the platform (LinkedIn and X, where operators post), format (text, carousel, short video), the post copy, the visual brief, the call to action and a sign-up link with UTM tags so results can be compared; 3) add a one-line goal per post (awareness, engagement, product education or lead generation) and what to measure at the end of the week. Tasks: the 7-day calendar with copy and links (content).

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Plan the week around when African educators are actually reachable, in formats that survive low data
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Timing and format decide whether a calendar earns attention. (1) Take the posting times and formats from public platform guidance for the audiences in the brief - Nigerian and African educators and bootcamp operators, mostly on phones - and pick the days and slots for the week from that, with the source and date for each choice rather than a habit. (2) Choose formats that work on a bad connection: short text, single image or a static carousel over auto-playing video, with the caption readable before the media loads. (3) Fill the seven days with the content types the goal names - awareness, engagement, product education, lead - and say which objective each day serves. Deliverables: the calendar table with time, platform, format, objective and source for each timing choice, and one line per day on why it is placed there.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Seven days, seven jobs: each day owns one campaign job
acceptedWorkstreams.description: A calendar is a plan only if every slot has a purpose. Approach: give each weekday one campaign job - teach a feature, prove it works with a real example, answer a question the audience actually asks, invite people in, share a community story, remind of the value, ask for feedback - then choose the format and platform that fits each job, with copy direction per slot and the Zedu page each entry links to. Claims stay limited to what the live pages support, and each link is checked on the day the entry is drafted. Tasks: the seven-day calendar with jobs, formats and copy direction (content), the link and claim check sheet (research).

rejectedIdeas.title: Plan the week around educators' real hours, with every slot verified before it goes out
rejectedIdeas.description: When a post lands decides who sees it: educators and bootcamp operators are likeliest to read in the evening or before classes, not at noon. Approach: write the seven entries around the audience's real day - morning reading, evening scroll, weekend planning - with a hook, format, platform and one call to action per slot, and a verification sheet recording that every link, product name and claim in the slot was checked against the live site the day before publishing. That keeps the calendar auditable rather than aspirational. Tasks: publishing table with audience reasoning (content), verification sheet (research).
